documents: Jia, Zhan & Kanamori (2022), The 2021 South Sandwich Island Mw 8.2 earthquake: A slow event sandwiched between regular ruptures, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2021GL097104 (published PDF, 8 pages)
pages_convention: printed journal pages (article pages 1 of 8 to 8 of 8, which coincide with PDF pages counted from 1)

entry.evidence: the deeper depths of the South Sandwich Island earthquake appear to contradict the shallow slip inferred from the global-spreading tsunami

steps.action: Report tide gauge records of the 12 August 2021 tsunami reaching about 20 cm at more than 10,000 km from the source in three oceans.
steps.quote: tide gauges measured peak amplitudes of ∼20 cm at over 10,000 km distance from the source

steps.action: State the provisional reading suggested by the global tsunami: a regular shallow tsunamigenic earthquake.
steps.quote: could be categorized as a regular shallow tsunamigenic earthquake

steps.action: Take the NEIC, GCMT and USGS catalog solutions (two events, depths 10 to 50 km, variable mechanisms), which point to a deep and complex rupture.
steps.quote: The early report (PDE) from the National Earthquake Information Center (NEIC) of the US Geological Survey listed two events within 3 min

steps.action: Run a W-phase moment tensor inversion; only a narrow 500 to 800 s pass band gave a satisfactory fit at 40 stations.
steps.quote: we attempted W-phase inversion

steps.action: Pose the question of the rupture process: resolve the depth-varying, non-planar rupture to reconcile the deep catalog depths with the global tsunami.
steps.quote: we need to analyze the rupture properties of this earthquake with flexibility in fault geometries

steps.action: Measure mB from vertical P waves at 54 global stations and MS from 20 s surface waves at 483 stations.
steps.quote: We used the vertical component P-waves recorded at 54 global network stations

steps.action: Compare mB and MS against the global mB–Mw and MS–Mw trends: the event falls 0.4 to 0.6 mB units and 0.5 MS units below them.
steps.quote: this indicates that these events, especially the mainshock, are deficient in short-period energy

steps.action: From its similarity to known slow tsunami earthquakes among the outliers, hypothesize a substantial slow shallow rupture component.
steps.quote: the South Sandwich Island earthquake probably involved a substantial slow rupture component at the shallow subduction interface

steps.action: Adopt the authors' multiple subevent inversion algorithm from earlier work, in which each subevent has its own timing, location, duration and mechanism.
steps.quote: Our subevent inversion algorithm represents a complex rupture with multiple simpler sources

steps.action: Design the inversion for a possible slow rupture: a unilateral Haskell finite subevent for any subevent longer than 100 s, Bayesian MCMC sampling, and subevents added until the fit is good.
steps.quote: we introduce a finite subevent with a unilateral Haskell rupture model with a constant rupture velocity

steps.action: Collect 58 teleseismic P, 43 SH and 12 three-component regional records, filtered in short, intermediate and long period bands.
steps.quote: This combination of short, intermediate and long period bands allows mapping the ruptures of different length scales simultaneously.

steps.action: Invert for a five-subevent model with posterior uncertainties. E1 and E2 are regular and propagate updip; E3 (Mw 8.16, about 180 s, about 1 km/s, 180 km southward, 14±5 km deep) has a low aspect ratio; E4 and E5 are regular and rotated in strike.
steps.quote: Our subevent model consists of five subevents that span ∼300 km along the trench

steps.action: Check the subevent locations and strikes against aftershock density and the curvature of the trench.
steps.quote: This rotation is consistent with the geometry of the curved South Sandwich Island trench.

steps.action: Compute the synthetic contributions of the regular subevents and of E3 in each frequency band: E3 barely excites short and intermediate periods but dominates the long periods.
steps.quote: The regular subevents E1, E2, E4, and E5 contributed almost all of the short and intermediate period waveforms

steps.action: Compare the band-limited contributions with the magnitude deficits: the weak short-period excitation of E3 explains the low mB and MS.
steps.quote: The diminished short period excitation explains the smaller-than-average mB and MS of E3

steps.action: Compare the subevent sequence with the NEIC, GCMT and their own W-phase solutions, mapping each onto subevents.
steps.quote: Figure 3d compares the overall rupture sequence determined by our multiple subevent inversion with the events determined by other methods.

steps.action: Place the 130 s centroid time shift on the centroid-delay versus Mw scaling relation, where it is anomalously long and close to the Guerrero 2002 and Java 2006 slow events.
steps.quote: the centroid time shift, 130 s, estimated from the half duration is anomalously long on the centroid time delay versus Mw scaling relation

steps.action: Keep the hybrid interpretation: deep regular rupture plus shallow slow tsunamigenic slip explain the large depth together with the global tsunami.
steps.quote: the South Sandwich Island earthquake appears to be a hybrid of deep rupture and slow tsunamigenic slip

steps.action: Invoke published low upper-plate rigidity models as a mechanism that accounts for the slow, short-period-depleted behaviour of E3.
steps.quote: Lower upper plate rock rigidity at shallow depths has been illustrated to produce tsunami earthquake-like properties

steps.action: Refine the claim: the slow slip may extend deeper than in traditional near-trench tsunami earthquakes, but its depth distribution is unresolved because of the moment–dip–depth tradeoff.
steps.quote: it is probably not confined in the near-trench depths like other tsunami earthquakes

tree.answer: Mw 8.2 event with globally spreading tsunami despite deep catalog depths
No; the rupture sequence is latent and inferred by waveform inversion
Resolve the spatiotemporal rupture sequence and its spectral character
Regular shallow tsunami earthquake versus deep regular thrust; resolved as a hybrid
Slow shallow rupture predicts mB/MS deficits relative to Mw and long centroid delay
Conditions found in a single live event
Consistent with other moment tensor solutions, aftershocks and trench geometry; no ablation reported
Kept: slow subevent sandwiched between regular ruptures

end.claim: The 2021 South Sandwich Island earthquake was a hybrid of regular deep and shallow thrust subevents and a hidden shallow slow Mw 8.16 subevent carrying about 70% of the moment; this explains its low mB and MS, its long duration and its global tsunami.

decisive_move.sentence: The multi-band subevent inversion, which included long-period regional waves and a Haskell finite subevent, revealed the slow E3 subevent that is invisible at short periods; without it there would be no claim.

gates.evidence: The slow-rupture hypothesis drawn from the mB/MS deficits (p. 4) shaped the inversion design: a Haskell long-duration subevent and long-period bands. It did not direct data acquisition, which used existing global records. The inversion could have returned no slow subevent, and the band contributions and the scaling comparison are independent consistency checks. No rival parameterization (for example, without a slow subevent) is reported as tested in the main text. Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling in a Bayesian framework

novelty_claims.quote: we revealed a hidden Mw 8.16 shallow slow event that happened between clusters of regular ruptures in the beginning and end
provides a more quantitative space-temporal pattern of this unusual sequence
represents an extreme example of the broad spectral behaviors of subduction zone earthquakes
the South Sandwich Island earthquake is among the biggest outliers from the general trend

limits: Single event; conditions found, not set. The supporting information (Texts S1–S2, Figures S1–S10, Tables S1–S2) was not supplied, so the W-phase details, MCMC settings, fits and uncertainty figures cited there were not inspected. No review file was supplied, though the acknowledgments mention two anonymous reviewers. The tide gauge data are shown but not modelled, for lack of bathymetry. Inference: no inversion without the Haskell slow subevent, or with alternative velocity models, is reported, so robustness to the parameterization is not shown. Sub-claim statuses: subevent timing, location, depth and moment are estimate_with_resolution, with the E3 depth at 14±5 km and the E3 strike and rake poorly constrained (Figure S9). The stress transfer explaining the aftershocks and outer-rise events is a 'presumably' (best_explanation, weak). The deeper extent of the slow slip is unresolved because of the moment–dip–depth tradeoff (none). Dynamic weakening as a trigger is speculation from the literature.

disagreements.target: NEIC, GCMT and USGS catalog locations and depths (10–50 km) for the sequence
disagreements.support: The authors attribute the scatter to interference between foreshock and mainshock waves and re-map the catalog solutions onto their subevents (Figure 3d).
disagreements.quote: This is probably caused by difficulty in locating the events accurately

disagreements.target: Initial NEIC report of a Mw 7.5 event at 47 km depth
disagreements.support: Long-period inversion reveals a shallow slow Mw 8.16 subevent that is hidden at short periods.
disagreements.quote: it was initially reported as a magnitude 7.5 event at a deep depth (47 km)

disagreements.target: Categorization as a regular shallow tsunamigenic earthquake from the global tsunami
disagreements.support: The inversion shows deep regular subevents combined with a shallow slow subevent, a hybrid rather than a regular tsunami earthquake.
disagreements.quote: could be categorized as a regular shallow tsunamigenic earthquake

disagreements.target: Traditional tsunami earthquakes confined to near-trench depths (Scholz, 1998; Kanamori & Kikuchi, 1993; Lay et al., 2011)
disagreements.support: E3 has a 14 km centroid and the tsunami was not devastating, which suggests the slow slip extends deeper; the authors note this is unresolved.
disagreements.quote: the slow component of the South Sandwich Island earthquake may have a broader depth extent than the traditional tsunami earthquakes

alternatives_considered.chosen: Multiple subevent inversion with flexible geometry
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Slip inversion on a planar fault
alternatives_considered.reason: A physical fault plane is hard to define given the diverse locations and mechanisms; aftershocks along a 400 km curved zone make a planar fault unphysical

alternatives_considered.chosen: Haskell unilateral finite source only for the long-duration (>100 s) subevent
alternatives_considered.reason: Possible slow rupture may propagate a long distance with strong directivity

alternatives_considered.chosen: W-phase inversion in a narrow 500–800 s pass band
alternatives_considered.reason: Complex interference of the waveforms of several events
